verdict.rationale: Highnote documents API-issued virtual cards with spend rules on dollar amount, authorization count, and MCC, plus per-transaction caps and cards that close automatically when a workflow ends. Together these approximate a scoped, limited-use card, but there is no named single-use card type and no exact-merchant lock; MCC is a category control, not a single merchant. Missing for 10: an explicit single-use card type that is invalidated after first use, a documented exact-merchant (merchant ID) lock, exact-amount matching rather than a cap, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can issue single-use and tightly scoped cards — one purchase, one merchant, an exact amount — so a leaked number is worthless the moment it's used

citations.quote: You can configure that logic on merchant category codes (MCC), dollar amount, authorization count, and more.
Issue cards per agent, workflow, or vendor via API. Each card closes automatically when the workflow ends.
Set velocity limits, merchant category restrictions, and per-transaction caps at the card, account, or program level.
